name: pedump
desc: Dump Windows PE files using Ruby
why: Dumping Windows PE headers from the terminal is a friendly way to see inside executables.

brief.what_it_is: pedump is a pure Ruby command-line tool that dumps the internals of Windows executables. You point it at a PE file (and it also handles DOS MZ, win16 NE, and EFI TE files) and it prints the headers, sections, data directories, resources, strings, imports, exports, version info, and packer/compiler guess to the terminal. Output defaults to a table and can be switched to bin, c, dump, hex, inspect, json, or yaml. It can also upload a file to the pedump.me website for an HTML rendering.
brief.why_it_exists: The README gives no separate problem statement. The homepage pitches it as a way to "dump your PE!", and the README describes it as a pure Ruby implementation of a win32 PE binary dumper.
brief.how_it_works: It parses the binary's structures in Ruby and prints them per section, selected with flags such as --pe, --sections, --imports, or --resources. Extraction flags such as --extract resource:VERSION/#1 or --extract section:.text write raw bytes to stdout, so they pipe into hexdump. Conversion flags such as --rva2file and --va2file translate addresses. Packer detection is heuristic, and --deep runs a slower scan.

commands_seen.context: Installs the pedump gem from RubyGems. The README's only install line.
Basic run on a PE file, which prints the default table output.
Prints the full option list, including formats, extract IDs, patch flags, and the -W upload switch.
Dumps the MZ (DOS) header of calc.exe.
Shows the 'Rich' header, which lists the Visual Studio build tools that produced the binary.
Lists the DLL's imported modules and functions.
Guesses the packer or compiler; the README's example result is 'MS Visual C v2.0'.
Mimics the output of the Unix 'file' command across a set of samples, with one line per file.
Extracts the VERSION resource by type and name, then pipes the raw bytes to hexdump.
Converts a file offset to a virtual address and prints the result in hex.

brief.install_notes: The homepage says you need Ruby 1.9+ with RubyGems installed, then run gem install pedump. No accounts, API keys, or special hardware are mentioned. The -W/--web option uploads your file to pedump.me, which needs network access. The news log says a 0.7.6 release fixed gem building from tar.gz for Homebrew users.
brief.standout: It is a pure Ruby PE dumper that covers old formats too (DOS MZ, win16 NE, EFI TE) and supports the .NET CLR. It also has an --extract mechanism for pulling out resources, sections, or data directories by name, RVA, or raw offset, plus a --packer-only mode that imitates the 'file' command.
brief.status: maintained. The README's News section has entries dated 2026.01.28 (versions 0.7.5 and 0.7.6), 2025.11.11, and 2025.03.16. The GitHub fetch returned only the README, so I could not see the last commit date.
brief.caveats: The -W/--web option sends your binary to a third-party site (pedump.me), which matters for proprietary or sensitive files. The README's dependency list was trimmed in 0.7.5 but still expects a working Ruby install. The README is short and points to the pedump.me site for examples, so I could not check how thorough the tool is against every format. The homepage lists a privacy policy, which I did not fetch.
